articles.title: Sophie Elizabeth Cunningham's inspiring story: From Missouri hardship to Indiana Fever stardom, resilience, basketball career, family, struggles and life beyond the WNBA
articles.summary: International Sports News: Explore the inspiring journey of Sophie Elizabeth Cunningham from her challenging childhood in Missouri to becoming an WNBA star with the Indiana Fever. Discover her resilience, family support, and the sacrifices made along the way.
articles.body: Sophie Elizabeth Cunningham’s story is an inspiration to all in terms of perseverance, family, adversity and her love for the game of basketball. She grew up in Columbia, Missouri, and her journey to becoming a respected WNBA player has included both amazing athletic achievements and painful personal experiences.Her journey added another chapter with the Indiana Fever, where Sophie Cunningham became known for her physical style, competitive energy and willingness to stand up for teammates. But her story is also about more than game stats, about childhood financial struggles, injuries, gruelling professional schedules, and meaningful connections with fans.Sophie Cunningham’s inspiring journey with Indiana Fever reveals resilience beyond basketballSophie Elizabeth Cunningham was born in Columbia, Missouri, into a family of sports enthusiasts. Her mother was a track athlete, her father a football player, and her sister Lindsey Cunningham also played basketball, so athletic competition was the norm.Cunningham had shown a rare sporting versatility from an early age. As a kid, she earned a black belt in taekwondo and was the first girl to make a field goal for her high school football team as a kicker. Although basketball was ultimately her primary sport, volleyball and other sports made up her athletic background.Cunningham was one of the most productive players in program history at the University of Missouri. She wrapped up her college career as the Missouri Tigers' all-time leading scorer with 2,187 points, and was also named an All-SEC performer.Sophie Cunningham overcame financial hardship before WNBA successThe Cunningham childhood was punctuated by a period of severe financial insecurity. The housing-market collapse and 2008 economic crisis hit her father’s contracting business hard and put a lot of pressure on the family.Accounts of the time describe the family losing the home to foreclosure while struggling to meet basic expenses. Financial resources became extremely limited, and relatives helped the family manage necessities such as food and transportation. Those experiences became key moments in Cunningham’s later reflections on perseverance.But the hardship did not stop Cunningham from growing as an athlete. As she went through high school and on to the University of Missouri, family support and a competitive environment remained front and center.Sophie Cunningham faced sacrifices beyond Indiana Fever gamesCunningham’s professional career has been more than the intensity of WNBA games. A demanding schedule of practices, travel, media obligations and competition often leaves little room for a personal life, especially when injuries or tough circumstances come into play.She’s spoken about the emotional toll of being a professional athlete, including times the WNBA schedule prevented her from attending funerals of people close to her. These experiences served as a stark reminder of the personal sacrifices that can be part of a career at the highest level of women’s basketball.Her physical style has brought tough moments, too. Injuries and rehab have been part of her pro experience, necessitating plenty of work off the court. Despite those setbacks, Cunningham has developed a reputation for toughness, competitiveness and a commitment to her teammates.Her relationship with the Indiana Fever fans has added another layer to that identity. Cunningham’s bond with the basketball community has been strengthened by gestures of young supporters, autographs and game-worn equipment. So her story is more than statistics: a combination of athletic accomplishment and perseverance through financial, emotional and physical hardships.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NBA trade rumor: Clippers controversy seemingly made Lakers $30 million target easy to land to bolster Luka Doncic’s roster
articles.summary: NBA News: The Los Angeles Clippers just got hit with one of the harshest penalties in recent NBA memory, and it's about to make life easier for their crosstown .
articles.body: The Los Angeles Clippers just got hit with one of the harshest penalties in recent NBA memory, and it's about to make life easier for their crosstown rivals. Five forfeited first-round picks later, the Clippers are shopping veterans to recoup draft capital, and Derrick Jones Jr. sits at the top of that list.For the Lakers, still finishing an offseason rebuild around Luka Doncic, that's a break they didn't expect. There is now talk that L.A. could add a familiar face from Doncic's Dallas days without giving up much at all.CategoryDetailPlayerDerrick Jones Jr.Current TeamLA ClippersRumored TeamLos Angeles LakersContract StatusFinal year of 3-year, $30 million dealSalary Cap Hit$10.4 million (2026-27)Trade LikelihoodModerate to highLatest Insider UpdateSean Deveney (Heavy): Jones is "most NBA trade-rumor ready"Potential ReturnNot specified in sources; reports indicate no first-round pick requiredHow could Derrick Jones Jr.'s pursuit finally be a jackpot for Lakers?The Clippers were docked five first-round picks after a nearly yearlong league investigation into salary cap violations, and the fallout has them scrambling to rebuild draft capital any way they can. Putting veterans on the block is the fastest route back to relevance in future drafts. “The player who is probably most NBA trade-rumor ready is Derrick Jones Jr., who has attracted attention across the league because he is a reliable defensive wing,” Heavy NBA insider Sean Deveney shared.The insider added, “The Clippers probably could not get a first-round pick for Jones, but there is a clamor for his services, and his expiring $10 million salary makes him an easy target.”Jones, 29, is in the final year of the three-year, $30 million deal he signed with the Clippers, carrying a $10.4 million cap hit for 2026-27. He averaged 10.1 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.4 assists a game this season while starting 45 games last year, per Clippers reporter Zion Trammel.Quick facts:Contract: 3 years, $30 million total, $10.4M cap hit for 2026-272025-26 stats: 10.1 PPG, 3.5 RPG, 1.4 APG, 0.9 SPG, 1.0 BPGCurrent status: On the trade block following Clippers' draft-pick penaltiesWing depth trade idea: Lakers land Doncic's old Dallas running mateThe idea centers on the Lakers using their need for wing depth to scoop up a player who already knows how to play alongside Doncic. Jones was part of the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, giving him real chemistry with the Lakers' franchise cornerstone.L.A.'s roster still has a hole on the wing even after an active offseason headlined by the addition of center Walker Kessler. Jones's mix of defensive versatility and athleticism fits that gap directly, and his expiring money makes him the kind of low-cost add-on teams chase near a deadline.The Clippers, meanwhile, are motivated to move him for a very different reason: their $10.4 million cap hit needs to go somewhere, and Jones profiles as an easier sell than L.A. Clippers reporter Zion Trammel noted the crowded frontcourt was already squeezing his role, writing he would likely have "a reserve role" after L.A. Clippers added Brandon Ingram and Rui Hachimura.What happens next in the Derrick Jones Jr. trade rumorsNot everyone thinks Jones is guaranteed to move. Clippers writer Tomer Azarly has reported Jones hasn't asked out and would even be open to a contract extension, which complicates any timeline for a deal getting done before opening night.The Lakers currently have just one tradeable first-round pick, and insiders believe they wouldn't need to spend it to get Jones. If that holds, the Clippers' bad month could turn into the Lakers' cheapest reinforcement of the offseason.Hypothetical trade structureLakers receive: Derrick Jones Jr.Clippers receive: Not clear as of now (reports indicate no first-round pick required)What the Lakers gain from this moveJones adds an established, switchable defender to a wing rotation that thinned out this offseason, plus a built-in rapport with Doncic from their Dallas run together. At an expiring $10.4 million, he wouldn't require the Lakers to touch their one remaining tradeable first-rounder, which keeps their long-term draft flexibility intact.What the Clippers get in returnThe sources don't spell out a return package, only that Jones "probably could not get a first-round pick" in the current market, per Deveney. For the Clippers, the real prize is shedding the $10.4 million cap hit as they work to rebuild draft equity lost to the league's penalties.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: LeBron James lands a $15 million payday in his latest career move, nearly 4 times his 76ers salary
articles.summary: NBA News: LeBron James is pulling in $15 million a year from a business deal that pays him more than the 76ers do. The four-time NBA champion's new partnership .
articles.body: LeBron James is pulling in $15 million a year from a business deal that pays him more than the 76ers do. The four-time NBA champion's new partnership with prediction-market platform Polymarket has turned into one of the more talked-about arrangements of the offseason, mostly because of how it stacks up against his actual playing contract in Philadelphia.The figures, first reported by Front Office Sports, put James well ahead of his $3.8 million salary for the coming season. The timing has also reignited chatter about why he passed on other suitors this summer, including a team that reportedly couldn't match the same financial flexibility.LeBron James' $15 million Polymarket deal dwarfs his 76ers salary by four timesLeBron James appeared in a Polymarket endorsement video alongside Derek Jeter and Eli Manning, plus a lineup of celebrities including Spike Lee, Reggie Bush and Alexandra Daddario. The campaign raised eyebrows given his past comments on gambling, and Polymarket later clarified his role would center on football, not basketball, since his DraftKings deal had just expired.Front Office Sports' Ryan Glasspiegel and Ben Horney broke down the numbers this week, reporting that James "will make more money from his Polymarket partnership than from playing for the 76ers." He's an endorser rather than an investor, and the length of the agreement wasn't disclosed, though sources described it as an ongoing arrangement involving social posts and other content. Jeter and Manning, by comparison, are reportedly earning smaller fees.Some fans have tied the deal to James skipping the Minnesota Timberwolves in free agency, since the state has moved to restrict prediction markets. The theory doesn't hold up well on its own, since James still took a pay cut to sign a two-year, $8 million deal with Philadelphia. The Timberwolves' tighter cap situation looks like the bigger factor in that decision.LeBron James reveals new career venture after Lakers exitAway from basketball, James has added another name to his business portfolio. He's now an investor in Mike's Red Tacos, a Southern California birria chain that started as a single San Diego food truck in 2021 and has grown into one of the region's most talked-about fast-casual concepts.The company is preparing to open its first Los Angeles-area location in Pasadena and has already signed development agreements for more than 300 franchise locations nationwide. James joins through Main Street Advisors, the investment group he's used for previous restaurant bets, including an early stake in Blaze Pizza and backing for Dave's Hot Chicken, which sold to Roark Capital last year for roughly $1 billion.Mike's Red Tacos is led by CEO Andrew Feghali and chairman Bill Phelps, both of whom helped build Dave's into a national chain, alongside founder Mike Touma. James has long been vocal about his love of Taco Tuesday, and this investment turns that public enthusiasm into an actual stake in the business.Between the two deals, James is proving his post-Lakers chapter isn't just about where he plays. It's also about where he puts his money, and right now, tacos and prediction markets both seem to be paying off better than expected.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: LeBron James’ former Miami Heat teammate Dwyane Wade drops cryptic comment on ex-Laker ahead of NBA season opener
articles.summary: NBA News: Dwyane Wade is not letting LeBron James' offseason exit from the Lakers fade quietly into the background. The Miami Heat legend addressed his former t.
articles.body: Dwyane Wade is not letting LeBron James' offseason exit from the Lakers fade quietly into the background. The Miami Heat legend addressed his former teammate's decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers, and his response hinted that there is a layer to the move most people have not connected yet.James is set to debut for Philadelphia on October 20 against the defending champions, Knicks, and the buildup has already turned into a talking point across the league. Wade, never shy about weighing in on his old running mate, chose this moment to stir the pot without giving away exactly what he means.Dwyane Wade reacts to LeBron James signing with 76ersDwyane Wade appeared on the "Conversations With Cam" podcast and was asked directly about James landing in Philadelphia. Rather than offering a simple take, the three-time NBA champion suggested there is more coming. "From a basketball standpoint, I thought it was a very strategic move at this point in his career," Wade said."I don't think we've seen the end of what this move is," Wade added, leaving the door open for speculation about what exactly he is referring to.Wade did not stop there. He called the decision a smart one for James at this stage of his career, pointing to the roster Philadelphia has built around him. The 76ers added Jaylen Brown in a trade that sent Paul George to Boston, then brought in Dean Wade and Anfernee Simons, giving James a starting lineup that also includes Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and Joel Embiid. Wade framed the fit as one that gives James a real path back to championship contention in the East.Dwyane Wade on LeBron James skipping Miami Heat reunionThe question Heat fans really wanted answered was why James never seriously circled back to Miami. Wade did not dodge it. "I think Miami would have been a good move as wel. but there's a lot of moving parts in that that needed to go right," Wade said.He acknowledged a reunion would have made sense on paper, especially with Miami retooling around Giannis Antetokounmpo and adding sharpshooter Klay Thompson, but he pointed out that too many pieces would have needed to line up for it to actually happen.The answer will not satisfy everyone in South Florida. Plenty of Heat fans still believe pairing James with Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo would have given him the best combination of talent and market appeal anywhere in his free agency search. Wade's comments suggest even he sees the logic in that argument, even if he ultimately backed James' choice to head to Philadelphia instead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: LeBron James’ reported $15m deal with Polymarket could trigger ‘really weird’ salary cap circumvention
articles.summary: LeBron James seems to be making up for the money he lost by signing up for Polymarket. After giving eight years of his career to the Los Angeles Lakers, LeBr...
articles.body:
LeBron James seems to be making up for the money he lost by signing up for Polymarket.

After giving eight years of his career to the Los Angeles Lakers , LeBron James finally moved on from the franchise as he signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers .

James took a historic $48.7 million pay cut to ensure he joins a team that has a shot at winning the NBA Championship without taking up too much of its cap space.

While James will make just $4 million per season with the Sixers, he has seemingly made up the difference with an off-court deal with Polymarket, reportedly worth $15 million.

NBA insider thinks LeBron James' Polymarket deal could set off a chain reaction

The NBA is currently more alert about its stars' endorsement deals due to Kawhi Leonard and the LA Clippers being found guilty of salary cap circumvention.

Keeping that in mind, NBA insider Brett Siegel believes James' new deal with Polymarket is technically within league rules, but it could set off a 'really weird' chain reaction.

"As far as my knowledge goes, this doesn't interfere with any CBA rules, but moving forward, these side deals players have with companies could directly lead to smaller contracts to help with cap relief, which in theory, is kind of like cap circumvention. Really weird times," Siegel wrote on X.

Since the introduction of the second apron, NBA teams have been forced to give smaller deals to their stars to avoid luxury tax.

Siegel believes James has set up the blueprint for how the future may look for the top stars to give their cap relief by signing massive endorsement deals, as long as they are within the current CBA rules.

articles.title: Polémica con el inédito contrato de LeBron: "¿Ha vendido su alma por 15 millones cuando ya tiene 1.000"
articles.standfirst: LeBron James, que acordó la mayor reducción salarial de la historia de la NBA, ganará más dinero gracias a su asociación con Polymarket que jugando para los Sixers
articles.summary: LeBron James, que acordó la mayor reducción salarial de la historia de la NBA, ganará más dinero gracias a su asociación con Polymarket que jugando para los Sixers
articles.body: LeBron James, fichaje estrella de los Sixers este verano, acordó la mayor reducción salarial en la historia de la NBA al firmar un contrato de 2 años y 8 millones de dólares con Philadelphia. El alero de 41 años ha pasado de cobrar 52,3 millones en su última temporada en los Lakers a los 3,8 que aceptado de los Sixers para el presente curso. LeBron James, que pierde 48,75 millones de una temporada a otra buscando el objetivo de optar al anillo en la Ciudad del Amor Fraterno, ha asumido una impactante disminución del 92% respecto a su salario anterior. En sus más de dos décadas de carrera en la NBA ha sumado 583,9 millones en contratos, pero su patrimonio es mucho mayor gracias a sus inversiones e ingresos por publicidad (tiene un lucrativo contrato vitalicio con Nike que le aporta 40 millones anuales). Otras empresas que apuestan fuerte por LeBron son Polymarket (en septiembre le ha firmado un contrato de 15 millones anuales como embajador de la casa de apuestas), PepsiCo, Richard Mille o Mattel (se convirtió en el primer atleta profesional en tener su propio muñeco Ken), AT&T, Beats by Dre, GMC, Rimowa y Walmart. Para ampliar y consolidar su fortuna LeBron James ha conseguido cambiar el pago de dinero por tener participaciones en empresas con las que colabora como Apple o Blaze Pizza. Según Forbes 'King' James cuenta con un patrimonio neto estimado en 1.400 millones de dólares. En plena vorágine de ataques a la actriz Sydney Sweeney por su controvertida colaboración con una casa de apuestas, en la que la acusan de hipersexualizar la imagen de la mujer y las deportistas, LeBron James está siendo muy criticado por su colaboración con otra casa de apuestas y el impacto que puede tener esa decisión en el mercado NBA. "¿LeBron James vendió vendió su alma por 15 millones cuando ya tiene 1.000 millones? No sé, aquí hay gato encerrado", denunció un aficionado en redes sociales. Brett Siegel aclaró en 'ClutchPoints' "que yo sepa, esto no infringe ninguna norma del convenio colectivo (CBA). Pero, de cara al futuro, estos acuerdos paralelos que los jugadores tienen con empresas podrían derivar directamente en contratos de menor cuantía para aliviar el tope salarial, lo cual, en teoría, equivale a eludir dicho tope", denunció Brett Siegel en 'ClutchPoints'. El analista destaca que "un jugador podría aceptar un contrato por una cifra significativamente menor sabiendo que tiene un posible patrocinio asegurado para compensar más de 10 millones de dólares... Luego, el jugador comunica al equipo que firmará por menos debido a esos acuerdos paralelos. Se hacen las gestiones pertinentes y el trato queda cerrado". Actualmente no hay indicios de que el acuerdo de James con Polymarket esté vinculado a los Sixers, y la NBA no cuenta con ninguna norma específica que prohíba a los jugadores promocionar mercados de predicción.
