articles.title: Super League Basketball: SLB set for 'most competitive season in 30 years'
articles.summary: The 2026-27 Super League Basketball season gets under way on Friday - and could be the most competitive in a generation, according to Newcastle Eagles owner Paul Blake.
articles.body:
"I've been involved for 30 years now and it's definitely the most competitive it's been, pretty much in all those 30 years," Newcastle Eagles owner Paul Blake said.

Excitement is building as British men's top-flight basketball prepares for a new season - with champions London Lions gearing up for a prestigious friendly against NBA opposition in Portland Trail Blazers next month.

Before that, though, the third season of the men's Super League Basketball - launched in 2024 after the British Basketball League folded - begins on Friday, as the Lions head to Bristol Flyers.

Last season, the Lions completed a domestic quadruple by winning the SLB Championship, SLB Playoffs, SLB Cup and SLB Trophy - and will be amining for more success when the campaign concludes in May.

This season, there will be 10 teams - up from nine - following the addition of Liverpool Basketball.

SLBW, the women's competition, starts on Saturday, 3 October.

'The quality is pretty much the highest it's been'

For many SLB clubs, there is optimism going into the new campaign - given some fine recent results and performances.

Manchester Basketball became the first British team to win a qualifying round match in Fiba's Basketball Champions League by beating German side Wurzburg Baskets earlier this week.

Bristol Flyers, meanwhile, will again compete in the European North Basketball League (ENBL), a competition in which Manchester finished runners-up last season.

The Lions are back in the EuroCup for a second straight season, EuroLeague's second-tier European club basketball competition - and are in good spirits after beating EuroLeague outfit Paris Basketball in pre-season earlier this month.

"The league is just getting more and more competitive all the time, so we know we'll be in for a fight again this season," Eagles owner Blake, who is also an SLB director, told BBC Sport.

"The quality of players that are now in the league across the teams top to bottom is, for me, pretty much the highest level it's been. It's extremely competitive."

'I've wanted to be in the NBA since I was six years old'

The Lions want to become one of world basketball's most recognisable clubs.

On 12 October, they will become the first British side to play an NBA team, when they face a friendly in the USA against the Portland Trail Blazers.

"I've wanted to be in the NBA since I was six years old. This is the closest I've ever been," Lions CEO Lenz Balan told BBC Sport.

"It's a really important signal in the basketball world, in the sporting world. This is the ambition. We are absolutely trying to be one of the best clubs in the world."

As well as looking to defend a domestic quadruple, the Lions will hope to improve on last season's EuroCup campaign.

While they did beat eventual runners-up Besiktas Gain in the group stage, they ultimately finished eighth out of 10 teams.

Balan is hopeful that their summer acquisitions, including the loan arrival of 2025-26 EuroLeague winner Keenan Evans, will help the Lions compete in Europe.

"We have ambitions to definitely outperform last year," added Balan.

"It's going to be tough, but these are some of the best players in the world - and I think most people in London and the UK recognise the level of competition that they're playing.

"We're just really focused on executing that vision, getting better and if we keep doing that, I think we're going to get some good results."

'Fans want to connect with the athletes'

Just 15 days after the SLB season tips off, SLBW will do the same.

Cardiff Met Archers host B Braun Sheffield Hatters, the defending championship and play-off winners, in the opening match on Saturday, 3 October.

At Cardiff, four players are salaried while also studying masters degrees at the university.

The rest of the team are made up of players on scholarships, postgraduate and undergraduate students and others that are balancing a career in basketball with full-time work.

"I think there's an opportunity to build something that people genuinely want to watch and follow," Archers head coach Stef Collins, a member of Great Britain's 2012 Olympic squad, told BBC Sport.

"Women's basketball has shown what is possible internationally, particularly with the growth we're seeing in leagues like the WNBA, NCAA College Basketball."

Collins wants SLBW to build on the recent Women's World Cup in Berlin, at which the United States earned a fifth successive title, beating France in the final.

"It was the most-attended World Cup in the modern era with over 230,000 fans in attendance," she said.

"For me, it's also about telling the stories of the players. They're not just basketball players - they're students, they're professionals, they're international athletes, they're role models. If we can showcase that properly, I think there's an exciting future for the Super league."

The WNBA, the independent women's equivalent of North America's NBA, has been among the pioneers in women's sports leagues across the globe.

In 2025, WNBA clips gained more than one billion views on Instagram, making it the most-followed women's sports league on that platform, which Collins feels can help SLBW on its path for development.

"The WNBA is a really good example of what happens when you give women's basketball a platform and make the players and their stories visible," she said.

"But I think there's also a lesson beyond the basketball itself. Women's sport has shown that fans want to connect with the athletes, their personalities and their stories.

"We shouldn't be afraid to market women's basketball differently and allow our players to be themselves."

articles.summary: At some point, the focus of the college basketball world will shift back from court courts to basketball courts.
articles.body:
At some point, the focus of the college basketball world will shift back from court courts to basketball courts.

Because actual basketball activities will soon be coming to a college campus near you. Before that happens, though, several prominent programs will get things going Midnight Madness-style—traditional fan showcases, albeit without the old 12 a.m. tip times.

Fresh off a 36-win effort and the program's first Final Four trek since 2001, the Wildcats will carry nothing less than championship expectations into this campaign.

They have a legitimate chance of realizing that lofty goal, too.

They're returning premier players like paint protector Motiejus Krivas and versatile wing Ivan Kharchenkov while fleshing out the core with impact transfers (Derek Dixon, JJ Mandaquit and maybe RJ Godfrey) and decorated freshman (Caleb Holt and Cam Holmes).

If head coach Tommy Lloyd's new club looks anything like his last one, the hoops world could be in trouble. Last season, Arizona was one of only two teams (along with national champion Michigan) to hold top-five efficiency ranks on both offense and defense, per KenPom.com.

Like a lot of John Calipari-coached teams, the Razorbacks are sort of starting from scratch. Their three leading scorers were all NBA draft picks—Darius Acuff Jr., Meleek Thomas and Trevon Brazile—so they had to get busy on the recruiting trail.

Fortunately, that's where Calipari cooks, and he might have served up the strongest freshman crop in the country.

As ESPN's Jeff Borzello observed, "there's a case for anywhere between two and four freshman to earn starting spots." Jordan Smith Jr., the No. 2 player on the 2027 NBA draft big board from B/R's Jonathan Wasserman , is a lock, but JJ Andrews (No. 5), Miikka Muurinen (No. 22) and Abdou Toure (No. 25) have arguments, too.

Throw in returning wing Billy Richmond III (No. 54) and transfers Jeremiah Wilkinson (17.4 points per game at Georgia) and Cooper Bowser (13.8 points on 76.6 percent shooting at Furman), and Arkansas might have the right blend of star power and depth to put together a special kind of season.

As per usual, the Blue Devils look absolutely loaded.

While they lost Cameron Boozer to the NBA, they kept his twin brother Cayden, along with seasoned floor general Caleb Foster, athletic wing Dame Sarr and powerful post player Patrick Ngongba II.

They added a number of notable newcomers, too. That includes celebrated recruits like Cameron Williams (a McDonald's All-American), Joaquim Boumtje-Boumtje (a 17-year-old who played at Barcelona) and Deron Rippey Jr. (an explosive lead guard), plus impact transfers led by John Blackwell, who averaged 19.1 points at Wisconsin last season.

Duke will play some really prominent non-conference games, so it should be obvious early just what kind of club this really is. If all goes according to plan, though, there might be enough talent for this school to capture its first national title since 2015.

articles.title: Xavi Pascual: "El Madrid tiene un ADN ganador, nosotros aún tenemos que crearlo"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Dubai Basketball habla sobre su equipo y sobre su rival en la SuperCup de la Euroliga
articles.summary: El entrenador del Dubai Basketball habla sobre su equipo y sobre su rival en la SuperCup de la Euroliga
articles.body: La temporada pasada, en plena descomposición de la plantilla del Barcelona, se supo que Xavi Pascual había sido tentado por el Dubai Basketball y que el entrenador catalán había aceptado. Aquello era más que el fichaje de un entrenador, en realidad se buscaba al capitán más apto para llevar los mandos de uno de los mayores transatlánticos de Europa. En historia, el Dubai es el equipo más pobre, por ser joven, de toda la Euroliga. En recursos, es uno de los más potentes. El primer año comenzó de forma más moderada y este año ha ido subiendo su inversión y su agresividad en el mercado hasta el punto de conformar una plantilla extraordinaria. Hay mimbres sobre la pista pero, sobre todo, en el banquillo. En Abu Dabi, donde el Dubai actúa como local y donde se enfrentará al Real Madrid, decían en el equipo dubaití sobre Pascual que "es el jefe, tiene la última palabra. Le han fichado para un proyecto a medio y largo plazo con la idea de que cada año nos haga mejores. Y el objetivo es ganar la Euroliga algún día", avisan. Xavi Pascual es más moderado, prefiere ir más despacio, controlando cada nuevo paso que da el equipo al que está dando forma: "Estamos intentando dar un paso más a un club de nueva creación que lo ha hecho muy bien hasta ahora y vamos a ver si conseguimos ir creciendo poco a poco. Estamos muy contentos de la organización, de cómo está funcionando todo, de cómo van estos primeros días, del equipo que hemos creado. Evidentemente, el potencial de otros equipos es absolutamente increíble, pero nosotros tenemos un equipo para intentar competir lo máximo posible", decía Pascual tras su último entrenamiento antes de enfrentarse al Madrid. El técnico catalán le da mucha importancia a esta especie de 'Final Four' que la Euroliga ha traído a Abu Dabi para arrancar la temporada: "Con las Supercopas siempre pasa un poco lo mismo. El ganador está muy contento, pero los perdedores siempre hablan de partidos de pretemporada. Pero la realidad es que cualquier cosa que jugamos la queremos ganar, todos los equipos. Estamos muy contentos de poder participar aquí, siendo un equipo organizador, contra tres de los cuatro mejores equipos de la temporada pasada. Por lo tanto, contentos de poder disputar esta Supercopa". Sobre la idea que quiere imponer en Dubái: "Vamos a intentar ser un equipo serio en las dos partes del campo, que pueda correr, que pueda jugar rápido en transición, que tenga dinamismo y que defensivamente sea un equipo sólido. Vamos a ver si poco a poco vamos creando esto. Un equipo que tiene que ir creciendo a base de partidos, seguro. Es un equipo nuevo, largo, en el que tenemos que adaptarnos todos, pero que vamos en la buena línea". A Xavi Pascual no le gusta hablar de retos en forma de títulos, aunque su mentalidad es que el equipo que esté en sus manos luche por cada uno de los torneos en los que participa. La Euroliga no es una excepción aunque a su debido tiempo. El equipo dubaití fue uno de los más activos en el mercado pero, ¿tiene el técnico todo lo que necesita?: "Cuando empieza la temporada ya no se puede mirar atrás. Esa es una regla que hay, y estoy contento con el equipo que tenemos. Da igual si durante el verano hemos intentado otras cosas y no han salido bien. Ya no importa, solo importa el presente. Como presente estoy contento con el equipo que hemos creado. Vamos a ser un equipo competitivo en cualquier cancha. El juego del baloncesto depende de los equipos, de quién juega mejor, de cómo empiezas los partidos muchas veces. En esta SuperCup, por ejemplo, vamos a jugar contra un equipo que tiene ADN ganador, y nosotros aún tenemos que crear muchas cosas".

articles.summary: Stephen Curry says he would rather re-sign with the Golden State Warriors than follow in LeBron James' footsteps by testing free agency next spring.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry says he would rather re-sign with the Golden State Warriors than follow in LeBron James' footsteps by testing free agency next spring.

Curry said Thursday on CNBC's Squawk on the Street that watching James weigh multiple free agency offers before signing with the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason was "not at all" appealing to him.

"I've always stated that I want to be a lifer with Golden State," Curry said around the 4:30 mark of the video below. "What we've built there, the fact that I get to run it back this year with Draymond [Green] and Coach [Steve] Kerr.

"All the contract stuff, this NBA thing from year-to-year is so crazy. Things change really fast. But I do know my interest and mission to state in Golden State and be competitive is there, and the contract stuff will take care of itself."

Curry is currently heading into the 2026-27 season on an expiring contract that has him scheduled to hit unrestricted free agency next spring.

The Warriors star has been eligible for a two-year, $136.7 million maximum extension since Aug. 29.

Curry expressed interest in re-signing with Golden State long before then, including after his team was eliminated from the play-in tournament in April.

He told reporters in his media availability immediately following an elimination loss to the Phoenix Suns he saw himself playing several more NBA seasons and would "for sure" be interested in signing an extension with the Warriors.

When asked for an update in negotiations earlier this month on the Dubs Talk Podcast, Curry said , "There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I'm pretty sure that's going to happen. The deal and contract stuff will happen in its right time."

Curry added he didn't expect contract talks would be a distraction from the Warriors' preparations for the upcoming season.

The Warriors didn't make any major changes to the roster this offseason beyond selecting forward Yaxel Lendeborg in the 2026 NBA draft.

The biggest change the Warriors are hoping to see next season will be better health. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still recovering from season-ending injuries, while Curry himself was limited down the stretch of the 2025-26 campaign with knee issues.

There is still a chance Curry could agree to a longer-term contract before the Warriors begin their push back to postseason contention. Curry has just over a month left to finalize a potential deal before the regular season tips off Oct. 21 at the Los Angeles Lakers.

articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "La SuperCup nos dirá cuál es nuestro verdadero nivel"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Madrid habla para MARCA horas antes de arrancar su temporada europea
articles.summary: El técnico del Madrid habla para MARCA horas antes de arrancar su temporada europea
articles.body: pedro Martínez y el nuevo Real Madrid entran en la escena europea por primera vez gracias a la SuperCup de la Euroliga, donde llegan como el vigente finalista de la Final Four. En Abu Dabi se medirán en semifinales al Dubai Basketball (este viernes, 19.00) y el sábado un partido más o por el tercer puesto o por el trofeo. Será una prueba exigente para comprobar la pretemporada de los blancos y el punto en el que el técnico catalán tiene al equipo días antes de empezar la competición oficial. Pedro Martínez atendió a MARCA antes de su último entrenamiento antes de arrancar la competición. "A nivel competitivo empieza ahora, sí, pero a nivel de trabajo creo que empezó el primer día que empezamos a entrenar, porque todo es importante y suma, los entrenamientos, los partidos, los amistosos y los de competición. Todo tiene su importancia y todo forma parte del camino". "Lo cierto es que es motivante y es exigente y nos pone delante del espejo para ver cuál es nuestro verdadero nivel y para ver qué tal van las cosas que hemos ido entrenando durante la pretemporada y desde ese punto de vista, creo que está bien. Pero también creo que no la deberíamos ver con la importancia que tiene realmente una Final Four cuando ya llevas muchos meses trabajando y tienes a los jugadores metidos en una dinámica de trabajo y obviamente tanto nuestros rivales como nosotros estamos en un nivel competitivo diferente". "Sí, sí. Porque además como entrenador siempre hay una parte muy importante de adaptación a la realidad que tienes. No sirve de nada quejarse de lo que no tienes y estoy satisfecho con lo que tenemos y sobre todo con la mentalidad que están teniendo los jugadores. Con todo esto esperamos construir algo que nos dé cierto éxito y sobre todo nos permita ser muy competitivos". "Creo que no habría que comparar. Son jugadores diferentes, clubes diferentes, momentos competitivos diferentes. Se trata de comparar con el Valencia de los últimos meses, el que jugó los Playoffs ante el Panathinaikos o el que ganó la Liga Endesa, y va a ser muy difícil llegar a ese nivel pronto. Con lo que habría que comparar es con el Valencia Basket de los primeros meses, y seguramente ese no era ni tan divertido ni tan redondo como el que jugó al final. Lo que hay que hacer es trabajar y tener paciencia e ir mejorando. Tratar de que todos se adapten, de que todo cuadre, de que todos los jugadores lo entiendan desde el primer día, es lo que nos gustaría que pasara, pero no va a ser tan rápido". "Trato de vivir al día, conozco cómo es el sistema de competición y conozco perfectamente las expectativas que tiene un club como el Real Madrid. Los medios que tenemos son muy grandes y no debemos escurrir el bulto los que tenemos responsabilidad. Pero yo prefiero no pensar a medio plazo y estar centrados en el presente, ahora mismo es la SuperCup, y luego centrarnos en el comienzo de la Euroliga. Y que nuestro trabajo nos lleve hasta donde nos tenga que llevar, sin ponernos más presión de lo que intrínsecamente ya tenemos como deportistas profesionales"

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Says Her Signature Shoes Are Best She's Played In After Loving Kobe's in New Video
articles.summary: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark commended the Nike design team on her first signature sneaker.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark commended the Nike design team on her first signature sneaker.

The three-time WNBA All-Star opened her media availability Thursday by discussing the new Caitlin 1s. Asked by one reporter to make a sales pitch for the kicks (6:50 mark), she said "they're probably the best looking shoe on the market" and called them the "best shoe I've ever played in." Clark added they eclipsed the Kobes she had worn regularly before.

Nike shared some of the process behind designing the Caitlin 1s and tailoring them to Clark's game. Alex Zerzan, a product line manager for Nike Basketball, explained one focus was building the shoe in a way that accentuates her movement on the perimeter.

The shoes don't hit stores until Oct. 1, but Clark has been wearing them throughout the WNBA season and during the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup.

Her performance has served as a great advertisement for the debut line. She's averaging a career-high 22.5 points and 8.4 assists through 36 games, with Indiana securing a third straight playoff berth.

articles.title: "Solo con vestir esta camiseta estás obligado a intentar ganar cualquier campeonato"
articles.standfirst: Campazzo y Feliz hablan sobre la SuperCup y la nueva temporada del Madrid.
articles.summary: Campazzo y Feliz hablan sobre la SuperCup y la nueva temporada del Madrid.
articles.body: Uno de los beneficios que tiene una Final Four es poder hablar con los protagonistas sin las restricciones de la temporada. Es poco tiempo y muchas veces tienes que elegir a tu objetivo, pero en este caso la casualidad hizo que estuvieran juntos Andrés Feliz y Facundo Campazzo para poder hablar de la nueva competición que están a punto de estrenar y de una temporada que para el Madrid se inicia con muchas caras nuevas y con una idea muy diferente de baloncesto. El Facu ya lleva muchos años en el Madrid, pero Feliz cumplirá su tercera temporada, la última de su contrato, y vista su progresión, todo apunta a que será también uno de los mayores pesos específicos en el equipo. Campazzo: "La veo bien, estamos trabajando mucho, estamos entrenando durante la pretemporada nuestra manera de jugar, jugadores nuevos, cuerpo técnico y entrenador nuevo, así que creo que esto va a ir de menos a más, esta parte de la temporada es donde quizás no se vea tan fluida la manera de jugar, pero creo que estamos trabajando para llegar bien a fin de temporada o a los partidos importantes, así que tratando también de que los nuevos se adapten lo más rápido posible y nosotros estar a la par también". Feliz: "Como ha dicho Facu, tratar de que las piezas nuevas se adapten lo más rápido posible al grupo y tratando de formar un buen equipo con tanto talento que tenemos en el equipo". Campazzo: Es una 'Final Four' bastante encubierta. A ver, no es lo mismo empezar ahora con un torneo tan importante como puede llegar a ser en mayo, que al final estás más rodado y tienes más partidos y demás, pero bueno, es un torneo, una supercopa de muchísimo nivel, de muchos equipos que pueden ser candidatos tranquilamente. Seguramente faltará alguno, pero van a estar ahí. Así que nada, viene bien, ya es el primer título oficial de nuestra temporada, y ya con vestir esta camiseta te obliga a hacer todo lo posible para intentar conseguirlo". Feliz: "Yo creo que el evento tiene muchísimo nivel, con equipos de alto rendimiento. Yo creo que también es una oportunidad para ver cómo acabas de finalizar la pretemporada, y como lo ha mencionado antes Facu, que es el primer título y la camiseta, pues eso nos obliga a competir y estar lo más arriba posible". Campazzo: "Bueno, bastante bien. Es bastante sencillo. Creo que en este punto de la temporada, al ser tan temprano, lo táctico es poco. Creo que quiere que empecemos solamente a hacer hincapié en las cosas que podemos controlar, que es la defensa, la energía, la intensidad, mientras que en ataque, la verdad que tenemos un equipazo, podemos anotar de diferentes maneras, diferentes posiciones, entonces creo que eso nos hace aún más peligrosos. Construimos nuestro ataque desde la defensa y creo que eso es lo que estamos trabajando ahora, sin muchas reglas, pero sí con mucha intensidad y las pocas reglas que tenemos, hacerlo lo mejor posible. Esto es un trabajo diario, de día a día, así que creo que el mejor Real Madrid se verá a medida que pase la temporada, pero creo que al tenerlo simple, eso a nosotros nos facilita mucho trabajo para aplicarlo lo mejor que podamos en la cancha" Feliz: "Es adaptación. Yo creo que vamos por un buen camino, tratando de adaptarnos a las ideas que quiere el nuevo entrenador. Yo creo que nuestra labor es seguir sus pasos, yo creo que, como todo el mundo sabe, es un entrenador de máximo nivel y nosotros como jugadores tenemos que adaptarnos a eso y brindar todo para formar un buen equipo".

articles.title: Michael Sweetney, former Georgetown great and NBA first-round pick, dies at 43
articles.summary: Sweetney played four seasons in the NBA after being drafted ninth overall by the Knicks in 2003.
articles.body:
Michael Sweetney, who played for the New York Knicks and Chicago Bulls after being a standout player at Georgetown, has died. He was 43 years old.

Sweetney's wife India announced the news on Thursday in a Facebook post .

"To know Mike Sweetney was love to him. No one loved him more and he loved no one more than his family," India Sweetney wrote. "His children were the light of his life, and he lived every day to give them the best life possible. He's been my best friend for 30 years and my husband for almost 20. I'm not sure what we or I will do without him."

Sweetney played three years at Georgetown and helped the Hoyas reach the Sweet 16 of the 2001 NCAA tournament. Over his final two seasons in college, he was a finalist for both the Naismith College Player of the Year and the John Wooden Award. During the 2002-03 season, he averaged 22.8 points, 10.4 rebounds, 3.2 blocks, 1.9 assists, 1.5 steals per game.

Sweetney was drafted ninth overall by the Knicks in 2003. He would play two seasons in New York before being dealt to the Bulls in a trade that included Eddy Curry, Tim Thomas and Antonio Davis. After two seasons in Chicago, he would go on to play for teams in Puerto Rico, Venezuela and Uruguay before retiring in 2017.

Following his playing career, Sweetney became a mental health advocate and spoke publicly about his own dealings with grief and depression, which he experienced early in his NBA career .

In 2019, Sweetney joined the Yeshiva University men's team as an assistant coach, while also coaching the varsity girls team at The Ramaz School.

"The world lost a giant today. I lost a close friend. The basketball world lost a beloved star," wrote Yeshiva head coach Elliot Steinmetz in a social media post . "Our Jewish community lost an ally and someone who knew exactly how to show up. "Mike Sweetney wasn't just a friend. He was family. When you needed him, he was there. Always. You didn't even have to ask."

articles.title: Caitlin Clark opens up on conversations with referees as she looks to avoid suspension for technical fouls
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark reveals how she now warns WNBA referees about her seven technical fouls, adjusting her approach to avoid a one-game suspension.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark says she has adopted a new approach to her conversations with WNBA referees as she attempts to avoid a suspension during the Indiana Fever’s final stretch of the regular season. Clark has accumulated seven technical fouls, leaving her one away from an automatic one-game suspension. With four regular-season games remaining, the Fever star said she now tries to remind officials that she wants to work with them when discussing calls. "I feel like the refs might also know I have seven technical fouls, so I always try to warn them," Clark said. "Like, ‘I’m working with you. I’m working with you. Like, let’s have a conversation.’" CAITLIN CLARK DROPS F-BOMBS AT OFFICIAL WHILE ARGUING FEVER WEREN'T GETTING THE SAME WHISTLE AS VALKYRIES The adjustment, Clark said, has changed her interaction with with referees. "I think it’s made my conversations with them more positive and more conversational in both ways for them and for me," she said. "I mean, I think it’s certainly been, like, a conscious effort about it, and I think it’s helped me play better basketball. It’s just, like, focus on what I need to focus on, and let the last play go. Like, you can’t go back in time and change things." Under WNBA rules, a player or coach receives an automatic one-game suspension after being assessed an eighth technical foul during the regular season. An additional suspension is imposed for every two technical fouls after that, while the totals reset for the playoffs. Clark briefly appeared to reach the eight-technical threshold during an Aug. 8 victory over the Chicago Sky. She was called for a technical after making contact with an official while going out of bounds, but the league rescinded it after the game, returning her total to seven and eliminating the suspension. Clark now has four regular-season games left to navigate. However, she noted that she effectively needs to avoid another technical only during the first three. A technical during Indiana’s finale would not remove her from that game, and there would be no subsequent regular-season contest for which she could be suspended before the total resets. "I really only have three more games to go because the fourth game starts — if I get a technical, I’m not kicked out of the game — and then it resets for the playoffs," Clark said. She added that the new interactions have made her "proud of herself." "I'm really proud of myself, but still three games to go. And I think it's helped me learn a lot about myself and the ways that I can impact my team, and, you know, how to communicate with the refs," Clark said. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Clark’s interactions with officials have drawn attention throughout her WNBA career. She has frequently expressed frustration over calls and the physical defense used against her, occasionally directing animated reactions toward referees. Clark received six technical fouls in each of her first two WNBA seasons, finishing one short of the league’s previous seven-technical suspension threshold both years. CAITLIN CLARK CALLS OUT REFEREES FOR FAILING TO CALL FOUL ON PLAY SHE SAYS GAVE HER A CONTUSION She has also acknowledged that her emotions can work against her. During her rookie season, Clark said she needed to do a better job of controlling her reactions because her team relied on her to remain on the court. That balancing act has continued as she has tried to preserve the intensity that defines her game without allowing disputes with officials to become a distraction. Indiana will then host the Washington Mystics before finishing the regular season with consecutive games against the Minnesota Lynx. Indiana entered the break at 26-14 and had already secured a playoff berth, although its final seed remains unsettled. Clark returns to the Fever after helping the United States win the World Cup in Berlin.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin’s return to Ole Miss comes with betrayal, lawsuits and memories of him trying to burn it all down
articles.summary: Trinidad Chambliss stayed at Ole Miss despite Lane Kiffin's alleged efforts to lure him to LSU, and now the Rebels are ready to wreck his return.
articles.body: OXFORD, Miss. - Just blocks away from a busy Ole Miss campus, residents of the small town of Oxford roamed 'The Square' on a Wednesday night that felt like a perceived calm before the storm that will have this city roaring over the next few days. An Ella Langley concert is scheduled for Thursday night, serving as an expensive kickoff party for a game that has drawn the attention of the entire college football world. Students strolled from campus to restaurants such as City Grocery, while visitors looking to stock up on Ole Miss gear stopped by Game Day Apparel for powder-blue hats featuring the phrase "Spot the Ball." MOUNTED POLICE, EXTRA PATROLS AND KIFFIN HATE: OXFORD PREPARES FOR OLE MISS-LSU GAME WITH EXTRA SECURITY Folks flocked to 'Off-Square Books' to hear my colleague John Talty discuss his new book on Lane Kiffin, which has already generated notably unfavorable reactions from those within Lane Kiffin's inner circle since its release. Inside Ajax Diner on Thursday afternoon, conversations shifted between the former head coach and the 2026 Ole Miss football team led by Pete Golding. SAM LEAVITT INJURY BOMBSHELL SENDS LSU-OLE MISS SHOWDOWN INTO CHAOTIC MODE, AS KIFFIN'S RETURN LOOMS But ... one talking point is persistent inside the landmark restaurant that opened in 1997. "We really need to win this game," one diner attendee said while clad in powder blue gear. "I can't imagine how that bastard will act if they [LSU] win." Maybe it'd be a different story if the outgoing coach didn’t try to burn it down There are plenty of people around Oxford who claim to know Lane Kiffin, whether through his six years in town or relationships built through late-night voice messages and text conversations. According to people who have spent time around him, the idea that Kiffin is a true "people person" remains debatable. "He didn’t really have use for you if there wasn’t something coming on the other end," Mike, from Oxford told OutKick. "Sure, he embraced the town, but he was spending more time in the yoga studios than the actual community. I'm not judging. He's a grown man, and he was single. "Obviously, you could tell he changed his life while here in Oxford. But, that doesn’t make him a good person, considering how he tried to burn this place to the ground on his way to LSU." OLE MISS FILES LAWSUITS AGAINST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYERS WHO LEFT FOR LANE KIFFIN'S LSU About that burning to the ground. If Lane had just left for Baton Rouge without all of the chaos that came with him trying to pigeon-hole his way into coaching Ole Miss during their playoff run, maybe the feelings would be a tad bit different. But, that's not Lane, especially when he doesn’t get his way. From assistant coaches pulling double-duty, flying back-and-forth between Oxford and Baton Rouge, to Kiffin just waiting for the Rebels to lose in the Sugar Bowl so he could at least feel better about his decision to leave during the most chaotic time in Ole Miss history, nothing was cordial about his exit. LANE KIFFIN GOES OFF SCRIPT: HULK HOGAN, OLE MISS AND SOCIAL MEDIA DOMINATE SEC MEDIA DAYS It's one thing to get a divorce. It's another to take things out of spite or try to empty the bank account on the way out of a marriage. "He's calling players while they are in meetings in hopes of negotiating a deal with their agents to get them to transfer once the season ended," one Ole Miss donor told OutKick. "The man was doing everything in his power to create obstacles for the Rebels during their CFP run." SEC FILES BOMBSHELL LAWSUIT AGAINST LSU, LANE KIFFIN WHILE PRO PLAYERS FIGHT FOR COLLEGE ELIGIBILITY IN COURT That even included quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who would return to Ole Miss for another season after being granted an injunction against the NCAA. Chambliss makes his return, through a court case. Those seem to follow Kiffin When the wheels were put into motion for Trinidad Chambliss to petition the NCAA for an additional year of eligibility, the thought process behind the move came from those within the Ole Miss athletic department. After alleging that a health issue during his time at Ferris State forced him into having to take a medical redshirt, the NCAA denied his waiver for an additional season. So, led by lawyer Tom Mars, after a call from Lane Kiffin, a lawsuit was filed against the NCAA in a small town court in Pittsboro, Mississippi. Inside A Louisiana Courtroom: SEC-LSU legal Circus Played Out Like A John Grisham Novel In Stunning Showdown We all know what happened from there, with Chambliss receiving his injunction by a local judge who shed a few tears while reading his order to the courtroom filled with supporters. The problem for Lane Kiffin was that he was thinking, before the case ended up in a courtroom, that Chambliss would follow him to Baton Rouge. Obviously, that part of the plan did not come to fruition, with Grove Collective founder Walker Jones putting together a deal for Chambliss that would keep him in Oxford, and away from the guy who tried his best to steal as much talent as possible from the Rebels roster. "This school was going to fight like heck to keep Trinidad and Kewan [Lacy]," another Ole Miss booster told OutKick. "We couldn’t lose those two guys, especially to Lane. This town has embraced those two, along with the entire team, like they are family. "Everywhere you go in Oxford, there are signs with their names or faces on it. When they decided to stay, we knew how much that bothered him [Kiffin]. I think in some different world, we would’ve paid them double, just to piss Lane off. He wasn’t going to get the entire family." LSU-OLE MISS SHOWDOWN INTENSIFIES AS TIGERS STAR SERVED WITH LAWSUIT PAPERS OUTSIDE FOOTBALL FACILITY And it seems as though court cases have just magically appeared around Kiffin, with the most recent battle taking place in Baton Rouge when Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright sued the NCAA for an additional season after exiting NFL preseason camps. As for Kiffin's interesting mind, even if LSU was not technically involved in the case, most of the football players involved in the Baton Rouge court were presumably headed to LSU. Well, there was maybe one player, Ethan Johnson, that supposedly went against the grain and ended up at South Carolina. "Somebody mentioned that when that one player [Johnson] decided to sign with the Gamecocks over LSU, ole Lane tried to get him taken out of that case in Louisiana," an Oxford local who had a relationship with Kiffin told OutKick. "Who knows, but it wouldn’t surprise me because that's how he operates. "It's his way or the highway. We learned that here. But, I'm not going to sit here and act as though we aren’t grateful for what he did for our program." All eyes on Oxford, as the college football world tunes in across the country Sure, some people simply want to watch the world burn. And this could be one of the wildest scenes college football fans have witnessed in quite some time. Ten months after Kiffin left Oxford on a private jet bound for Baton Rouge, he will return to Vaught-Hemingway Stadium as the head coach of the LSU Tigers. This will not be his first trip back to Oxford since leaving Ole Miss. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! But Friday afternoon through Saturday night will bring a different kind of energy — one built on the pageantry, resentment and unpredictability that make college football so compelling. There will be profanity. There will be middle fingers directed at Kiffin. But, there will also be a top-ten showdown that will have major ramifications for the season. The main character of this story will arrive on Friday afternoon to a destination being kept secret in the name of security. articles.title: El español Sergi Oliva formará parte del cuerpo técnico de los Hawks
articles.standfirst: El técnico, con experiencia en los Sixers, los Jazz y los Blazeres, ejercerá como asesor de estrategia y desarrollo de baloncesto en el equipo que dirige Quin Snyder
articles.summary: El técnico, con experiencia en los Sixers, los Jazz y los Blazeres, ejercerá como asesor de estrategia y desarrollo de baloncesto en el equipo que dirige Quin Snyder
articles.body: El entrenador español Sergi Oliva se unirá al cuerpo técnico de los Atlanta Hawks como asesor de estrategia y desarrollo de baloncesto, tras pasar las últimas cuatro temporadas como asistente del mánager general en los Portland Trail Blazers. Además de Oliva, los Hawks también anunciaron la incorporación de Ettore Messina como consultor de entrenamiento y de Jason Love como entrenador asistente para el banquillo que dirige Quin Snyder. El español conoce de cerca el trabajo de Snyder, para quien ejerció de asistente durante dos temporadas en los Utah Jazz (2020-22). Antes, Oliva había trabajado seis meses en los Philadelphia 76ers, en los que llegó a ser vicepresidente de estrategia. Su experiencia más reciente fue en los Portland Trail Blazers y llegó a dirigir a los Rip City Remix de la NBA G League en la temporada 2024-25. El movimiento de los Hawks aporta veteranía al banquillo para una franquicia con mucho talento joven y que el año pasado alcanzó los 'playoffs' por primera vez desde 2023.

articles.title: Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry - Official Trailer - IGN
articles.summary: Take a look at the Official Trailer for Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry, a sports documentary centered around NBA legend Stephen Curry, distributed by Disney. Fans can witness the career of the iconic player with Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry, in theaters exclusively in IMAX on October 9.On the verge of his record-extending 4,000th career three-pointer, four-time NBA champion and two-time MVP Stephen Curry reflects on the upbringing, mindset and work ethic that have made him among the most legendary artists of our time. The film captures Curry leading up to and throughout one remarkable game, weaving together his generational artistry with perspectives from other innovative artists – including Viola Davis, Rick Rubin, Patti Smith and Jon Batiste – showcasing how his singular vision has permanently transformed the game of basketball. This state-of-the-art production utilized 21 IMAX-certified cameras to capture the urgency and emotion around this historic single day and single game. When Curry hit his 4,000th career three-pointer, it wasn’t just another record – it was something the league had literally never seen before. Curry entered the home game at Chase Center against the Sacramento Kings needing just two threes to reach the unprecedented milestone of 4,000 career three-pointers. Curry became the first player in NBA history to reach this historic milestone. The Warriors went on to win the game 130-104.“Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry” is directed by Gotham Chopra; produced by John Turner, Meghan Cirillo, Nick Frew, Erick Peyton and Sharla Sumpter Bridgett. Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry releases exclusively in IMAX theaters on October 9.

Take a look at the Official Trailer for Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry, a sports documentary centered around NBA legend Stephen Curry, distributed by Disney. Fans can witness the career of the iconic player with Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry, in theaters exclusively in IMAX on October 9.

On the verge of his record-extending 4,000th career three-pointer, four-time NBA champion and two-time MVP Stephen Curry reflects on the upbringing, mindset and work ethic that have made him among the most legendary artists of our time. The film captures Curry leading up to and throughout one remarkable game, weaving together his generational artistry with perspectives from other innovative artists – including Viola Davis, Rick Rubin, Patti Smith and Jon Batiste – showcasing how his singular vision has permanently transformed the game of basketball.

This state-of-the-art production utilized 21 IMAX-certified cameras to capture the urgency and emotion around this historic single day and single game.

When Curry hit his 4,000th career three-pointer, it wasn’t just another record – it was something the league had literally never seen before. Curry entered the home game at Chase Center against the Sacramento Kings needing just two threes to reach the unprecedented milestone of 4,000 career three-pointers. Curry became the first player in NBA history to reach this historic milestone. The Warriors went on to win the game 130-104.

“Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry” is directed by Gotham Chopra; produced by John Turner, Meghan Cirillo, Nick Frew, Erick Peyton and Sharla Sumpter Bridgett.

articles.title: Angel Reese's Teammate Suffers Season-Ending Setback as Atlanta Dream Announce Concerning Update
articles.summary: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are steadily becoming a serious contender to win the WNBA championship as they sit at No. 4, just behind defending champion...
articles.body:
Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are steadily becoming a serious contender to win the WNBA championship as they sit at No. 4, just behind defending champions Las Vegas Aces . And after the World Cup break, you would think that head coach Karl Smesko's side would be fully fresh to prepare for the business end of the season. However, the team has suffered the opposite fate, as All-Star center Brionna Jones is out for the remainder of the season with an injury.

"The Atlanta Dream announced today that center Brionna Jones will miss the remainder of the 2026 season after sustaining a left leg injury against the Connecticut Sun on August 13. Jones is expected to make a full recovery."

The Dream announced Thursday, as reported by ESPN's Holly Rowe on X .

This comes ahead of the Dream's matchup with the Sun, the same team against which Jones picked up a left leg injury at the Mohegan Sun Arena last month on August 13, 2026. The mishap occurred in the second quarter, when Jones slid over to assist in defending Nell Angloma, who was about to drive to the basket. The two met each other in the paint, as Jones successfully blocked the shot before Angloma could get it off.

Jones immediately began hopping as soon as she landed after blocking the shot. And that was the end of her season with the Dream, as Jones went back to the locker room at the 8:56 mark after playing just four minutes, finishing with one rebound, one assist, and one block.

Just three days before she sustained the injury against the Sun, Atlanta Dream Karl Smesko revealed that they were being cautious about the WNBA veteran's time on the hardwood.

"She's coming off an injury and a surgery and a rehab and hadn't played for a really long time. So, we are being kind of conservative with bringing her along, but she's doing well. We're hoping to be able to progress her to more time on the court."

Smesko was referring to the meniscus tear on February 6 while playing in Europe for the USK Praha in Czechia. That injury took a toll on Jones's 2026 WNBA regular season as she had to wait almost half the season before making her debut on July 17, barely a week ahead of the 2026 All-Star Game.

Now, with this current injury putting an end to her season, Jones's final stats stand at 9.3 points on 52.9% shooting and 6.1 rebounds. Although those stats may not look impressive when taking an entire season into context, it's crucial to note that she played only 9 games before getting sidelined for good.

That means Jones's absence will be a big miss for the Dream and their frontcourt. The franchise already made adjustments, signing DeWanna Bonner ahead of the World Cup break for some much-needed experience in the playoffs. Moreover, No. 13 overall pick Madina Okot has absorbed Jones' minutes since her injury as well.

The Dream frontcourt will now rely on Angel Reese even more than before, who has become the main pillar in the Dream's defense. Reese is currently the best rebounder in the league, averaging 12.4 per game. She has also levelled up in steals, ranking third in the league with 1.8 per game. Reese's defensive efforts are visible to all, which is probably the reason she is one of the favorites to win the Defensive Player of the Year award.

The Atlanta Dream's current record stands at 26-14, with four games left to play. They are currently fourth in the standings, one place above Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever . With two upcoming games against the New York Liberty , the Dream's frontcourt depth will be tested significantly, but it will also give Karl Smesko a chance to build a solid defense ahead of the playoffs.

articles.title: The Pistons’ Quietest Move Could Be Their Best
articles.summary: Oklahoma City never found the minutes for one of its best shooters, and Detroit just took him. #Pistons
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons did not land a blockbuster star this offseason. Most of their moves were marginal. But the one that could matter most is also the quietest: the Pistons sending two future second-round picks to Oklahoma City for Isaiah Joe . Joe spent four of his six NBA seasons with the Thunder, a team with an embarrassment of riches, and he never averaged even 22 minutes a game there. In Detroit , the window for real opportunity is finally open.

Oklahoma City Never Had Minutes for Isaiah Joe

No team has matched the depth of the modern Oklahoma City Thunder over the past decade. Joe was not stuck in the middle of the rotation because he could not play. He was one of many Thunder players sacrificing minutes they would have gotten on most other NBA rosters. Last season, Joe averaged 11.1 points while shooting 42.3% from three on six attempts a game . He never shot below 40% from deep in his Thunder tenure.

Joe measured 6'4 1/2 in shoes at the 2020 NBA Combine, with a 6'7 1/2 wingspan and an 8'5 standing reach , so he has the length to cause problems defensively. He is also a more explosive athlete than his reputation suggests. All of that complements players like Cade Cunningham and Ausar Thompson , and it makes him a candidate to stay on the floor in crunch time.

Cade Cunningham Will Create His Best Looks Yet

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander might be the best player in the world. But respectfully to SGA, Cade Cunningham is arguably the best passer in basketball. Per Cleaning the Glass , 43% of his teammates' made shots come off Cunningham's assists. Sports Info Solutions had him leading the NBA in potential assists at 19.5 per game last season , and his playmaking shows up the same way at Bball-Index .

Malik Beasley is the template. He made a career-high 319 threes on a career-best 41.6% from deep in his one season next to Cunningham . With expanded opportunity in Detroit, Joe has the same chance to set new career bests. Shooting has been Detroit's Achilles' heel in the Cunningham era, so it could be hard to take a shooter of that efficiency off the floor. And since the Pistons still need guards who can handle the ball , he will see reps there too.

All of the signs point toward Joe being a clean fit. Thunder coach Mark Daigneault called him a first-class professional and one of the best shooters in basketball after the trade, and a player who came up in that environment should handle high-pressure minutes. He might not be the next Grant Hill, but he could be Detroit's next Tayshaun Prince. Players like that are paramount to winning championships, something Joe already did in Oklahoma City in 2025 .

articles.title: Chus Bueno: "Aún no hemos recibido ninguna propuesta de la NBA"
articles.standfirst: El CEO de la Euroliga pasa revista los temas de actualidad justo antes de la SuperCup
articles.summary: El CEO de la Euroliga pasa revista los temas de actualidad justo antes de la SuperCup
articles.body: la Euroliga vive continuamente en el alambre, pero sabe caminar sobre él como nadie. Mientras mantiene el pulso con la NBA sobre el nuevo orden del baloncesto, en Europa se dedica a expandir sus competiciones, la Euroliga y la EuroCup, y está a punto de dar a luz a una nueva criatura: la SuperCup. La nueva competición en la que participarán Olympiacos, Fenerbahce, Real Madrid y Dubai Basketball, reúne a tres de los cuatro mejores equipos de la pasada temporada, más el anfitrión. Comenzará a jugarse este viernes y el sábado, alrededor de las 21.00, conoceremos a su primer campeón. Chus Bueno, el CEO de la Euroliga, el hombre al timón, reunió a un grupo de medios europeos, entre los que se encontraba MARCA, para hablar de este formidable estreno, de la Euroliga y de las relaciones con la NBA con respecto al intento de desembarco de la competición estadounidense en Europa. "La SuperCup no es solo un torneo de pretemporada como muchos piensan. No, es una competición. Es una gran competición y queremos tomarla muy en serio. Nunca tendrás una segunda oportunidad para ser el primer ganador de la competición. Esta no es una edición más, es la primera. Y puedo ver que todo el mundo está muy concentrado. E incluso cuando camino y hablo con los jugadores y los entrenadores puedo sentir la tensión de los partidos". "La SuperCup no es algo original de la Euroliga, hay supercopas en casi todas las ligas nacionales, pero no nos inspiramos en la NBA Cup. Queríamos hacer más cosas, nuestra misión es traer negocio y activos a la Euroliga. Y, para mejorar nuestro producto pensamos en una SuperCup que sirviera para despertar a todos de cara a la nueva temporada. Pensamos que era una buena idea, da promoción y da la oportunidad de un nuevo trofeo para los equipos". "El verano ha sido muy movido con fichajes y transacciones porque todos quieren tener a los mejores, y eso me encanta. Esa tensión de querer ganar la competición es buena. Pero tenemos que hacerlo según las reglas. Y según eso, no se puede hablar con un jugador que tiene contrato. Primero hay que hacerlo con el club al que pertenece y si te da permiso, te acercas al jugador. Si esto no pasa, abrimos una investigación y es lo que hicimos y hablamos con todas las partes. Al final hubo acuerdo". "Yo soy el CEO y por eso busco activos y negocios para la competición pero también actuamos como sheriff para cuidar que se sigan las reglas y el proceso". "Habrá dos conferencias y se pasará de 38 a 34 partidos. Pero aún estamos trabajando en la confección de esas conferencias. El departamento de competición está preparando diferentes modelos geográficos con distintas líneas de separación. Ante todo queremos respetar las rivalidades locales porque tienen mucho valor": "Conozco bien a Adam (Silver), a Mark Tatum y a George (Aivazoglou). Son amigos. Estuve en la NBA casi 13 años. Así que hablamos sobre lo que podemos hacer juntos. La fragmentación diluye el valor no solo institucionalmente, sino en los medios, en los patrocinadores, en los fans y crea fricción porque de alguna manera vamos a competir". "Así que creo que todo el mundo entiende que si podemos eliminar la fricción y la fragmentación, sería mejor. Pero al mismo tiempo, la proposición que la NBA ha dicho de querer compartir el espacio, no la hemos recibido todavía": "Y esa proposición, la que sea, tiene que tener sentido para la Liga y para los equipos. En Europa hay un ecosistema creado con varias ligas europeas y luego las domésticas. Y sé que lo saben y estamos hablando de cómo encontrar un modo para crear una buena competición juntos que pueda armonizar el ecosistema también. Pero veremos. Aún no hemos recibido nada". "Los equipos están contentos con la Euroliga.Tenemos un plan. Están emocionados por convertirse en franquicias. Están emocionados por la expansión. Tenemos 12 propuestas vinculantes de 800 millones en dinero para los clubes. Y vamos a decidir esto en menos de dos o tres semanas. Y vamos a ir a 24 equipos. Potencialmente vamos a ir a 28, 30 equipos en los próximos tres o cuatro años para una segunda expansión. La gente está emocionada. Tenemos dinero, tenemos competición, tenemos talento, tenemos todo y estamos creciendo muy rápido. Y ahora vamos a hacer estas expansiones, más mercados y con SuperCups y cosas así más activos": "Tenemos los activos y los equipos y seguimos y la NBA viene con una gran oportunidad porque también quieren unirse a Europa. Debemos estar abiertos a explorar. No es un movimiento defensivo. Tenemos un plan y vamos a competir. Tenemos un gran producto y tenemos grandes planes". "Creo que en todas las negociaciones tienes que escuchar a la otra parte y ver cómo se puede encontrar un modo de poner ambas ideas en un buen lugar. Lo que no veo es que la NBA quiera imponerse como si fuera una conquista. No creo que sea el modo correcto y sé que ellos los saben": "En los seis meses transcurridos desde mi incorporación, hemos logrado unir a todos los equipos en torno a un plan que han respaldado plenamente, incluyendo todos los aspectos que acabo de mencionar; y cuando se cuenta con un buen plan, la NBA deja de ser la única alternativa. Ya tenemos un plan. No se trata de pensar: "Vaya, no tenemos otra opción que irnos a la NBA". No, tenemos un plan excelente". "Ellos no son la alternativa; nosotros tenemos un gran plan. Por supuesto, siempre exploramos vías para mejorar y para crecer". "Pero estamos abiertos a la NBA y a cualquier otra propuesta que surja; siempre estamos abiertos a nuevas oportunidades y hablamos con mucha gente —muchos inversores— dispuestos a aportar grandes sumas de dinero. Sin embargo, nuestra postura es que no se trata de dinero, ya que obtendremos fondos a través de las expansiones. La pregunta clave es: ¿qué aportan ustedes? ". "No voy a negar que la NBA podría ser, potencialmente, un gran negocio si llegamos a un acuerdo, porque sabemos lo que la marca, el aspecto operativo, el marketing y la propiedad intelectual aportan, pero tiene que tener sentido. Es muy sencillo: no hacemos malos tratos. Así que no vamos a hacer un mal trato. Tiene que ser un buen trato". "Creo que hemos mejorado nuestra posición y nuestra capacidad de negociación, pero al final del día, aunque eso es importante para el proceso, lo que realmente importa es el acuerdo en sí. Podrías ofrecer el mismo acuerdo independientemente de tu poder de negociación, simplemente porque consideras que es justo y adecuado para el ecosistema del baloncesto; podrías hacerlo por convicción y con generosidad, en lugar de adoptar una postura de "tengo mejores opciones, así que voy a presionarte más". "Sí, tal vez estemos en una posición más fuerte, pero un buen acuerdo es aquel que beneficia al baloncesto en su conjunto. Lo hemos hablado: no se trata solo de los tres actores clave de la negociación —algo en lo que la NBA coincide—; debe ser un acuerdo que beneficie a todo el ecosistema. Si cierras un trato que deja fuera a cinco equipos, estos seguirán compitiendo y creando rivalidad; si el acuerdo incluye a trece actores del ecosistema, habrá muchos otros capaces de competir y crear una liga paralela". "Por tanto, el acuerdo debe funcionar para todo el ecosistema. Si se hace para trece, quedan fuera otros once o doce que podrían fundar otra liga mañana mismo. Tenemos una oportunidad única: en lugar de fragmentar aún más el mercado, podemos construir juntos una gran estructura piramidal".

images.caption: Chus Bueno durante una entrevista. ÁNGEL RIVERO

articles.title: Muere Michael Sweetney, la estrella universitaria a la que una depresión impidió brillar en la NBA
articles.standfirst: El ala-pívot, exjugador de los Knicks y los Bulls, fallece a los 43 años tras tener que lidiar con problemas mentales y sobrepeso desde su año de novato
articles.summary: El ala-pívot, exjugador de los Knicks y los Bulls, fallece a los 43 años tras tener que lidiar con problemas mentales y sobrepeso desde su año de novato
articles.body: Michael Sweetney, exjugador de los Knicks y los Bulls, ha fallecido este jueves a los 43 años. Fue su propia esposa, India, quien anunció la noticia a través de una publicación en las redes sociales. Se desconocen las causas de la muerte del ala-pívot de 2,03 metros. Sweetney fue una estrella en la Universidad de Georgetown, donde en su última temporada, la 2002-03, tuvo unos bestiales promedios de 22,8 puntos, 10,4 rebotes, 3,2 tapones, 1,9 asistencias y 1,5 robos por partido. Eso le hizo estar entre los candidatos a prestigiosos galardones como el premio Naismith al Jugador Universitario del Año y subir posiciones en las previsiones del draft. Finalmente, fue seleccionado por los Knicks en la novena posición en 2003. Sin embargo, a su llegada a la NBA nunca pudo cumplir con las expectativas debido a problemas de salud mental. Su padre falleció justo antes de comenzar su temporada de rookie y eso le hizo caer en una profunda depresión. Sumado a la falta de minutos, Sweetney acabó sufriendo trastornos alimenticios que le llevaron a un exagerado sobrepeso. Con sólo 2,03 metros de altura, Sweetney llegó a rondar los 150 kilos cuando jugaba en la NBA. En etapas posteriores, varias decenas más. Pese a ello, jugó dos temporadas en Nueva York antes de ser traspasado a los Bulls en un intercambio que incluyó a Eddy Curry, Tim Thomas y Antonio Davis. Entre sus dos etapas, disputó 233 encuentros en la Liga estadounidense con promedios de 6,5 puntos y 4,5 rebotes en 15,5 minutos en pista. Cuando se cerraron las puertas de la NBA, el ala-pívot se convirtió en trotamundos. Militó en equipos de China, Puerto Rico, República Dominicana, Venezuela y Uruguay antes de retirarse en 2017. Después de dejar el baloncesto, basándose en su propia experiencia, Sweetney trabajó para exponer las enfermedades mentales y habló públicamente sobre lo que había sufrido al inicio de su carrera en la NBA, cuando todo lo que prometía como jugador en la Universidad se quedó en poco debido a la depresión que sufrió.

articles.title: LeBron James, Kevin Hart Planning YouTube Golf Collaboration, Negotiations Nearing Finish Line
articles.summary: Two of the biggest names in their respective industries are teaming up for a new golf show.
articles.body:
Two of the biggest names in their respective industries are teaming up for a new golf show.

Per Front Office Sports' David Rumsey , NBA icon LeBron James and actor/comedian Kevin Hart are planning a collaboration on a YouTube golf showdown, with the negotiations nearing the finish line.

"We've got a big match coming up," Hart said. "We're just giving ourselves some time to both improve so that when we show up, there's a nice amount of juice to amplify the concept of the game."

2017 NBA Re-Draft Gives Teams the Ultimate Do-Overs 🏀

Every NBA Team's Top Breakout Candidate This Upcoming Season 😀

With the rise of golf YouTube channels over the past few years, James and Hart have both gotten into making videos separately. James started his channel over the summer, with his first video being a vlog of his golf trip with members of the championship-winning 2016 Cleveland Cavaliers team.

James' channel has garnered over 600,000 subscribers, with his first video hitting nearly 3 million views. He's since posted two more long-form videos documenting his golf battles.

Hart started his YouTube channel last month and has picked up more than 80,000 subscribers and 2.5 million views on his first video.

James got into golf a few years ago, and it quickly became one of his favorite pastimes. Before delving into the YouTube world, his social media account was filled with photos and videos of him playing golf.

"It's hard as s--t," James said last September (h/t ESPN's Kalan Hooks ). "... I wanted a challenge, man, and I like being uncomfortable. Golf is like one of the few places where I can go where I don't get bothered as much."

Hart is also relatively new to the sport but appears to be making some progress, based on his YouTube videos.

Golf has long been one of the more inaccessible sports, but YouTubers have inspired a new generation of golfers by playing it in a non-traditional way from what has been the standard for years.

James and Hart are arguably the two biggest names to have created YouTube channels dedicated to golf, and their eventual showdown should draw quite an audience.

When the two will tee up together remains to be seen.

"We want people to tune in and watch," Hart said. "But right now we said let's give ourselves a certain bandwidth of space to get better."

articles.title: Saddiq Bey, Pelicans Agree to $55.5M Contract Extension Ahead of NBA Season, Updated Salary Cap
articles.summary: Saddiq Bey impressed for the New Orleans Pelicans last season, and he will reportedly be with the Western Conference team for the foreseeable future.
articles.body:
Saddiq Bey impressed for the New Orleans Pelicans last season, and he will reportedly be with the Western Conference team for the foreseeable future.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported the Pelicans and the forward agreed to a fully guaranteed three-year, $55.5 million contract extension that features a trade kicker and locks him in with New Orleans through the 2029-30 campaign.

According to Spotrac , the Pelicans have $217.1 million in salary cap allocations for the 2026-27 campaign.

Knicks walk back ticket pricing increase

Bey entered the league as the No. 19 overall pick of the 2020 NBA draft and was an All-Rookie First Team selection for the Detroit Pistons.

Detroit eventually traded him to the Atlanta Hawks during the 2022-23 campaign, but he missed the entire 2024-25 season because of a torn ACL. Given the severity of the injury, there were no shortage of questions when he joined the Pelicans for the 2025-26 season.

Bey averaged a career-best 17.7 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game while shooting 45.1 percent from the field and 36.7 percent from three-point range last season. Only Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III averaged more points per game for the Pelicans.

The Villanova product clearly showed enough for the front office to believe in him moving forward, and the Pelicans responded accordingly to make sure he remains with the team for the foreseeable future.

Seeing how Bey is still just 27 years old and now has some familiarity in place with some of his Pelicans teammates, it is reasonable to expect him to be even better over the course of this contract.

If he is, perhaps New Orleans can take a leap in the Western Conference and compete for a playoff spot.

articles.title: Pelicans forward Saddiq Bey agrees to 3-year, $55.5 million extension after successful comeback from ACL tear
articles.summary: Bey posted a career season last year with the Pelicans.
articles.body:
Saddiq Bey made a successful return from a torn ACL last season. Now he's being rewarded for it.

The New Orleans Pelicans forward has agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . The deal reportedly includes a trade kicker.

Bey was previously under contract for one more season on a salary of $6.4 million.

Bey entered last season as an unknown after tearing his left ACL toward the end of the 2023-24 season, ending his time with the Atlanta Hawks . He wound up spending the next season rehabbing his knee with the Washington Wizards on a three-year, $20 million deal, and was traded to the Pelicans last summer before ever making his debut in D.C.

Bey's first season with New Orleans saw him post a career-high 17.7 points per game on career-best shooting efficiency numbers, along with 5.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game.

That performance didn't prevent another rough season for the Pelicans, who missed the playoffs at 26-56, but the 27-year-old Bey still showed he was a piece worth building around.

After helping lead the United States to the gold medal in the 2026 FIBA World Cup, the Atlanta Dream forward was dominant during Thursday's 103-59 victory over the Connecticut Sun.

In fact, she made franchise history with a 30-10 performance and league history with another double-double:

Here is a look at Reese's final stat line in her first WNBA game since Aug. 30:

Reese also tallied a 30-10 game when she posted 31 points, 14 rebounds and four steals during a victory over the Phoenix Mercury on Aug. 22.

Thursday marked her 30th double-double of the season, which was the WNBA record. It is a surprise at this point if she doesn't finish with a double-double as a rebounding machine who has taken steps as a scorer as well in Atlanta.

She entered Thursday's game averaging 16.1 points per game, which is a career-high mark before she scored 30 against the Sun.

While Reese was one of five players for the Dream who scored in double figures, she was also the only one who scored more than 10. Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard, Madina Okot and Te-Hina Paopao all scored 10 points each.

Things didn't get out of hand for Connecticut until the second half, as Atlanta was up 10 points at halftime. Yet the Dream dominated the third quarter 31-11 and never looked back for a game that featured very little drama.

Atlanta is now 27-14 on the season, which is fourth place in the WNBA standings and just a half-game behind the third-seeded Las Vegas Aces.

If Reese continues to play at this high of a level, the Dream could climb into that No. 3 seed and be in favorable position come playoff time.

articles.title: WNBA Playoff Picture 2026, Official Bracket Scenarios After Wings vs. Sparks
articles.summary: The Dallas Wings improved their positioning in the 2026 WNBA playoff picture with a 97-77 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on Thursday night.
articles.body:
The Dallas Wings improved their positioning in the 2026 WNBA playoff picture with a 97-77 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on Thursday night.

Here's a look at the updated standings and bracket scenarios following the victory.

2. Golden State Valkyries, 29-11 (2 GB)*

While all eight playoff spots have already been clinched, teams are still looking to improve their seeding as the postseason draws closer.

The Wings entered Thursday's action in a three-way tie with the Washington Mystics and New York Liberty before emerging victorious over Los Angeles.

Dallas won largely due to the efforts of star guard Paige Bueckers, who scored a team-high 19 points on 8-of-13 shooting against the Sparks.

Although the Wings moved above New York with the win, Washington was also able to take down the Chicago Sky on Thursday. The Mystics own the tiebreaker over Dallas, putting them in the No. 6 seed as the Wings sit at No. 7.

The Atlanta Dream picked up a 103-59 win over the Connecticut Sun on Thursday as well. The Dream now hold the No. 4 spot in the playoff picture, although they're just 0.5 games back from the Las Vegas Aces at No. 3. Atlanta is also a mere 0.5 games up on the Indiana Fever at No. 5, though.

All three teams will be attempting to clinch one of the top four playoff spots in order to earn home-court advantage in the first round.

Higher up the WNBA standings, the Minnesota Lynx are trying to secure the No. 1 seed in the league for the second consecutive year.

The Lynx, led by standout rookie Olivia Miles and star forward Napheesa Collier, only need to win two of their final four games in order to clinch the top seed heading into the playoffs.

articles.standfirst: La pívot española se convirtió en la jugadora más joven en la historia de la WNBA y en la única de 20 años en la liga en alcanzar los 50 triples en su carrera
articles.summary: La pívot española se convirtió en la jugadora más joven en la historia de la WNBA y en la única de 20 años en la liga en alcanzar los 50 triples en su carrera
articles.body: La WNBA volvió este jueves a la acción después de casi tres semanas en un parón coincidiendo con la Copa del Mundo de baloncesto femenino disputada en Alemania, en la que Estados Unidos se proclamó campeón al derrotar a Francia en la final. Varias de las campeonas del mundo disputaron partidos este jueves, como Angel Reese, que completó 30 puntos y 10 rebotes en la paliza de las Atlanta Dream a las Connecticut Sun por 103-59 en el encuentro inaugural de la jornada. Además, Rhyne Howard rompió el récord de triples en una temporada con 129, al anotar desde el perímetro en su noveno intento. En Dallas, las Wings derrotaron a Los Angeles Sparks por 97-77 con el quinto triple-doble (13-11-12) de la temporada de Jessica Shepard, mientras que la campeona del mundo Paige Bueckers terminó con 19 puntos. Las Washington Mystics se impusieron a las Chicago Sky por 80-110 y las Phoenix Mercury 91-94 a las Portland Fire. Las Vegas Aces cerraron la jornada con su victoria por 77-114 en su visita a las Seattle Storm, con 35 puntos de Jackie Young, titular contra Francia, y 29 de A'ja Wilson, que renunció a la selección para cuidar de su físico. Para las Storm, la valenciana Awa Fam fue titular y terminó con 5 puntos, 9 rebotes y 2 asistencias. Su compañera en la selección española y jugadora de las Mystics, Alicia Flórez, firmó 8 puntos en la victoria de Washington.
